comment: kiln.world, game-program wraps (0.2.0-dev.28, chapter 06a): the program scheduler's live path and the players mask that decides whether a world's program slices run inline on the world's thread or as tasks on the game's workers. Wraps themselves need no symbol of their own (they swap the update pointer of a program-table entry, entry+0x28, with the world/programs.* constants); these resolve the scheduler for the threads report and the lab's parallel switch. SimStep (it sets storage+0x518 = 1 at entry, so it always takes this path) calls RunInitPrograms, then StepPrograms in a loop: StepPrograms' prologue decides parallel per world kind (server: the u16 players mask at storage+mask != 0; prediction: never; client: always), cuts slices and runs ProgramRunner (types/ProgramRunner) inline or posts SliceTaskFn tasks. The players mask holds bit (id-1) mod 16 for every live player entity (ids 1..1023). Same bytes on server 26430253 (f0d824be) and client 26430625 (5d9ef2f1); svn 1273043 (d7baa768) has another prologue frame size, which the second StepPrograms strategy (the kind dispatch, 0x22 bytes in) does not depend on. world.slice_record (dev.29): the engine slice record's entry, rows and archetype layout, read in types/ProgramRunner, for WhenArchetype's scheduler-stable source.

@world/ProgramRunner.slice.comment: types/ProgramRunner's prologue (rcx storage, rdx the engine's slice record, r8 index, r9 worker area): the slice record's program-table entry (mov rbx,[rdx+entry]; the runner calls [entry+0x28], the update), its end and first rows (mov r15d,[rdx+end]; sub r15d,[rdx+first]: the job's entity count). The bytes types/ProgramRunner is found by, then the three reads.

@world/ProgramRunner.layout.comment: types/ProgramRunner hands the slice's archetype layout and group to the column setup (mov r9,[rdi+group]; mov r8,[rdi+layout]; rdi = the slice record): the layout is the archetype object whose bitset is at +0 (the same object as an entity record's world/entity.layout; out/06a-program-wraps/client-static/r5). Then the stores of the column setup's frame.

world.slice_record.comment: kiln.world's archetype source for a wrap stage (0.2.0-dev.29): a checked typed link around types/ProgramRunner keeps the engine's slice record (rdx) on the thread for exactly that runner call (restored on return, a skip by a later hook and unwind); a stage reads the slice's layout from it, checked against the entry and row count the trampoline ran with. Installed when a stage first asks for its slice's archetype.
